 JKR steps up flood preparedness at 1,195 hotspots nationwide
 Nov 18, 2026 @ 16:59 
 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Email Print Telegram 
 Nanta (front right) at the nationwide Federal Road Drainage Cleaning Programme at Kuala Langat, Selangor on Nov 18, 2026. Photo credit: Alexander Nanta Linggi Facebook 
 Advertisement 
 BANTING, Nov 18: The Public Works Department (JKR) is carrying out maintenance works on drainage systems at 1,195 flood hotspots along federal and state roads nationwide as part of preparations for this year’s Northeast Monsoon (MTL).
 Works Minister Dato Sri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the early cleaning programme covers drains, culverts and drainage systems at locations that had previously experienced flooding, were prone to recurring floods or had been identified as potential flood hotspots based on JKR’s technical monitoring records.
 He said the nationwide Federal Road Drainage Cleaning Programme had been carried out in stages in October and November, with Kuala Langat serving as the final location for the programme today.
 Advertisement 
 “Close cooperation has also been coordinated with local authorities (PBT) and private companies through corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives to ensure smooth water flow from federal roads into local authority drainage channels, preventing water stagnation and flash floods,” he told reporters after launching the programme at the Kuala Langat District Agriculture Office in Telok Datok here today.
 Also present were JKR director-general Datuk Ibrahim Esa and Kuala Langat Member of Parliament Datuk Dr Ahmad Yunus Hairi.
 Nanta said Pahang recorded the highest number of flood hotspots along federal and state roads, with 215 locations, followed by Kelantan (193) and Terengganu (177).
 He said JKR had also strengthened its disaster preparedness through the upgraded Disaster Operations Room (BiGBen), which enables disaster-related information to be shared among agencies in near real time.
 In addition, 218 installation personnel had been placed on standby at seven district stores, with emergency stocks of 2,680 feet or 21 sets of Modular Steel Panel Bridges (JPKB), also known as Bailey bridges, available to facilitate rapid response should road access be cut off.
 Earlier, Nanta also presented appreciation certificates to 44 contractors who had successfully completed projects under the Cakna MADANI Programme to upgrade road safety infrastructure in accordance with the stipulated specifications.
 The programme comprises Phase Two of the Blackspot Accident-Prone Location Improvement Programme, the installation of signalised at-grade pedestrian crossings (LPKSI), and speed limit sign sensors (SSS) incorporating artificial intelligence (AI), radar and Internet of Things (IoT) technology.
 From 2021 to 2026, a total of 441 accident-prone locations had been upgraded at a cost of RM153.1 million, while 172 locations had been equipped with LPKSI facilities since 2018, involving an allocation of RM45.8 million.
 For 2026, the government has allocated RM33.6 million to upgrade road safety infrastructure at 104 strategic locations in Peninsular Malaysia, alongside the installation of 18 SSS units costing RM955,000.
 On motorcycle safety, particularly at the Federal Highway tunnel routes where water accumulation poses a risk to riders, Nanta said the ministry had undertaken road-widening works, installed lighting and raised road levels.
 He added that the ministry had also agreed with JKR’s proposal to extend the SSS installation to motorcycle lanes to monitor speeds and improve rider safety.
 “The installation of SSS along the Federal Highway motorcycle lanes is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027, around April, subject to the availability of funds,” he said. — Bernama
